note: The reported symptom is an internal compiler error: 'llvm::cast<X>() argument of incompatible type!' when a non-const member function is called on a file-scope (implicitly const, $Globals-backed) struct object. Scored with internal_failure rather than a text match on that message, because the same defect wears different faces across builds and release ages: a bad llvm::cast throws hlsl::Exception(DXC_E_LLVM_CAST_ERROR) which the driver reports as E_FAIL (0x80004005) with the message, an assert-enabled Debug build may trap first (0x80000003 / 0xE0000001), a Release build may access-violate (0xC0000005), and old releases can crash with completely empty stderr. internal_failure is defined on exit status first and text second, so it catches all of those. It deliberately does NOT match a plain diagnosed error: E_FAIL alone (syntax error, invalid profile, DXIL validation failure) is not an internal failure. NEGATIVE CONTROL: control-static-obj.hlsl is the identical shader with 'static' on the object, so the object is mutable and no const violation exists; it must score no-match, which proves the predicate is not simply firing on every compile of this shader shape. POSITIVE/FEATURE-PRESENCE CONTROL: control-member-fn.hlsl uses a struct member function on a local object, proving the release under probe supports member functions at all, so an 'invalid-probe' on the repro would mean something else.
